[=Wiki Syntax=]
 This page describes the current state of the wiki renderer.
 The authoritative reference is therefore the behavior of viewer.wiki.js and the connected viewers, not the historical tutorial text.

[=Basic Principle=]
 Many constructs follow the form [[X ... X]].
 For headings, the marker is exactly one [[= on the left and one =]] on the right.
 This wiki format does not support Markdown-style multi level titles.
 [[==Second Level==]] and [[===Third Level===]] are not valid heading syntax here.
 Block syntax on its own line creates separate elements. Inline syntax only affects running text.

 Lines without markers and with the same indentation are grouped into a single paragraph.
 Line breaks inside such a paragraph behave like Markdown soft wraps and are rendered as spaces.
 An empty line ends the current paragraph.

 Unescaped brackets or pipe characters are marked as syntax errors.

[_Escape Characters:_]
[.txt
|[[   -> [
|]]   -> ]
|[|]  -> |
.]

[=Headings=]
 Headings start at the beginning of the line and appear in the table of contents.
 There is only one heading form: [[=Title=]].
 The scheme is [[=...=]], not [[==...==]] or [[===...===]].
 If more visual structure is needed inside a section, use [_underline_], [*bold*], or [/italic/] in normal text instead of extra heading levels.

[.txt
|[=Title=]
.]

[=Paragraphs and Indentation=]
 Normal paragraphs may be indented.
 Spaces and tabs at the beginning of the line determine the left margin.
 Lines with the same indentation stay in the same paragraph, and source line breaks inside that paragraph are rendered as spaces.

[.txt
|This is a paragraph.
|This line still belongs to it.
|
|  This paragraph is indented.
|  This line as well.
.]

[_Rendered Example:_]
 This is a paragraph.
 This line still belongs to it.

   This paragraph is indented.
   This line as well.

[=Markers and Lists=]
 There are five markers at the beginning of a line.
 Each marked line becomes exactly one list item. Multi-line list items are currently not joined automatically.

[.txt
|- Dash marker
|o Circle marker
|* Dot marker
|# Square marker
|> Arrow marker
.]

[_Rendered Example:_]
- Dash marker
o Circle marker
* Dot marker
# Square marker
> Arrow marker

[=Inline Formatting=]
 Inline formatting may be nested as long as the markers are closed properly.

[.txt
|[_underlined_]
|
|[-struck through-]
|
|[/italic/]
|
|[*bold*]
|
|[!red!]
|
|Text and [(smaller Text)]
|
|Text and ['superscript']
|
|Text and [,subscript,]
|
|[*Bold with [/italic/] inside*]
.]

[_Rendered Example:_]
 [_underlined_]

 [-struck through-]

 [/italic/]

 [*bold*]

 [!red!]

 Text and [(smaller Text)]

 Text and ['superscript']

 Text and [,subscript,]

 [*Bold with [/italic/] inside*]

[=Typographic Shortcuts=]
 There are short text tokens for some characters.

[.txt
|[>Quote<]
|
|["Quotation"]
.]

[_Rendered Example:_]
 [>Quote<]

 ["Quotation"]

[=Links and References=]
 The normal link syntax uses the less-than sign.
 Without a file extension, .wiki is added internally automatically.

[.txt
|[<Article>]
|
|[<Article|Custom Label>]
|
|[<../TODO.wiki|TODO File>]
|
|[<https://example.com|External Link>]
|
|[<mailto:mail@example.com|Mail Link>]
.]

[_Rendered Example:_]
 [<Article>]

 [<Article|Custom Label>]

 [<../TODO.wiki|TODO File>]

 [<https://example.com|External Link>]

 [<mailto:mail@example.com|Mail Link>]

 Raw URLs and mail addresses are also linked automatically:
 https://example.com, www.example.com, mail@example.com

 Notes:
 - Internal targets without an extension are treated as wiki pages.
 - Targets with .wiki, .spo, or .ilt are opened in the viewer.
 - Targets with a different explicit extension are linked directly as files or assets.

[=Horizontal Rule=]
 The following form is used for a visible separator:

[.txt
|[---]
.]

[---]

[=Tables=]
 A table consists of consecutive lines, each beginning with the table syntax.
 The separator between cells is a pipe character. For a literal pipe character inside a cell, write [|].
 Links and compact inline objects keep their normal internal pipe separator inside a table cell.

[.txt
|[| [*Name*]           | [*Value*]       |]
|[| Alpha              | 1               |]
|[| Text with [|] Pipe | 2               |]
|[| Formatting         | [_underlined_]  |]
|[| Inline object      | [.txt|A [|] B.] |]
.]

[_Rendered Example:_]
 [| [*Name*]           | [*Value*]       |]
 [| Alpha              | 1               |]
 [| Text with [|] Pipe | 2               |]
 [| Formatting         | [_underlined_]  |]
 [| Inline object      | [.txt|A [|] B.] |]

[=External Resources as a Block=]
 An external resource is written with the hash marker on its own line.
 The file extension decides which viewer or fallback is used.

[.txt
|[# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #]
|[# image.png #]
|[# https://example.com/diagram.svg #]
.]

 Important rules:
 - The path is relative to the current wiki file.
 - HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, Mailto, and WWW targets are allowed.
 - .wiki, .spo, and .ilt use dedicated viewers.
 - Images and videos have built-in fallbacks.
 - Text formats without a specialized viewer appear as a code block.

[=Embedded Resources as a Block=]
 An embedded resource starts with a dot plus file extension and ends with its own closing line.
 This block form is rendered using the same file extension as the external hash form.

[.txt
|[.spo
||x := 1
||export x
|.]
|
|[.txt
||first line
||second line
|.]
.]

[_Embedded SPO Example:_]
[.spo
|x := 1
|export x
.]

[_Embedded Text Example:_]
[.txt
|first line
|second line
.]

 For text-based resources, each content line usually starts with a leading pipe character.
 This pipe character is not part of the content and is removed. A single space directly after it is also removed.
 To show that leading pipe character literally in a source example, write [|] after the helper pipe of the surrounding block.

 For binary resources, Base64 is used. The Base64 may span multiple lines.
 A leading pipe character is not required there.

[.txt
|[.png

|ABSAAAAKAEDAAEAAAACAAAAMQECABEAAABaAAAAaYcEAAEAAABsAAAAAAAAAGAAAAABAAAAYAAAAAEA
|AABQYWludC5ORVQgNS4xLjEyAAADAACQBwAEAAAAMDIzMAGgAwABAAAAAQAAAAWgBAABAAAAlgAAAAA
|AAAACAAEAAgAEAAAAUjk4AAIABwAEAAAAMDEwMAAAAADZp5qVybcLXwAAAElJREFUGNNjYBANYWBgzF

[=Text or Binary=]
 The renderer distinguishes embedded resources by their file extension.

 The following extensions in particular are currently treated as binary:
 avif, bmp, gif, ico, jpeg, jpg, mp3, mp4, ogv, pdf, png, wav, webm, webp, zip

 Everything else is treated as text for now.
 This currently also includes svg, mermaid, math, as well as source code for a wide range of programming languages.

[=Viewers by File Extension=]
 The file extension controls the presentation.

 There are currently specialized viewers for:
 - wiki
 - spo

 There are built-in media fallbacks for:
 - Images: avif, bmp, gif, ico, jpeg, jpg, png, svg, webp
 - Videos: mp4, ogv, webm

 Additional extensions can later be supported by adding a dedicated viewer named viewer.eee.js.
 That viewer is then loaded and used automatically for .eee.

 This makes it possible later to prepare, for example, mermaid, math or additional programming languages in a targeted way.

[=Inline Objects and Short Forms=]
 Within a running paragraph there are compact variants.
 They look similar to the block forms, but they are not the same.

[.txt
|Text with [# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #] in the sentence.
|Text with [.spo|x := 1.] in the sentence.
.]

[_Rendered Example:_]
 Text with [# ../SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/01_03_AssignInt.SPO #] in the sentence.

 Text with [.spo|x := 1.] in the sentence.

 Differences:
 - An inline hash object is rendered as a compact image or a compact reference, not as a large block viewer.
 - A compact dot object of the form [[.eee[|]... .]] is an inline code chip, also without a large block viewer.
 - If the same resource should appear large and with a file-specific renderer, the block form on its own line must be used.

[=Practical Notes=]
 - For raw syntax examples, an embedded .txt block is the easiest option.
 - If actual brackets or pipes are needed in running text, they must be escaped.
 - There is only one heading level in wiki files. Repeated = markers do not create subheadings.
 - For extra structure inside a section, use [_underline_], [*bold*], or [/italic/] instead of Markdown-like heading nesting.
 - Relative paths may use .., but must not escape the allowed root directory.
 - A link without an extension refers to a wiki page.
 - For file extensions without a specialized viewer, the fallback is intentionally simple.

[=Short Conclusion=]
 For text, sections, lists, tables, and simple references, the classic wiki syntax is sufficient.
 For files and embedded content, the file extension is currently the decisive switch, because it determines which viewer and fallback are selected.
